infra: GitHub REST API (ETag-conditional, file-based JSON cache)

subsystems.name: Deterministic collector
subsystems.what: tools/collect.ts (~696 LOC): reads seed/repos.toml, walks git log, calls GitHub API, computes LOC/stack/cadence/authorship/similarity, emits data/profile.json with no LLM or randomness — same inputs produce identical JSON

subsystems.name: ETag-conditional GitHub REST client
subsystems.what: tools/lib/gh.ts: typed GhClient with file-based JSON cache, ETag If-None-Match, 304 short-circuit, rate-limit fallback to stale cache, paginator, stats-endpoint retry loop

subsystems.name: Pure SVG chart library
subsystems.what: tools/lib/charts.ts (~384 LOC): hand-built stat cards, horizontal/vertical bar charts, heatmap matrix, Gantt timeline — no chart lib, no browser, deterministic bytes, rasterized via @resvg/resvg-js

subsystems.name: Cross-repo similarity engine
subsystems.what: tools/lib/similarity.ts: pairwise Jaccard (stack tags + deps) + cosine (workflow vector) composite scorer with union-find clustering at configurable threshold

subsystems.name: Stack + tooling detector
subsystems.what: tools/lib/stack.ts: parses JS/Python deps from package.json/pyproject.toml/requirements.txt, detects package manager/linter/bundler/monorepo tool, infers architecture shape (monorepo vs single, apps/, packages/)

subsystems.name: Commit cadence analyzer
subsystems.what: tools/lib/workflow.ts: by-DOW/by-hour histograms, longest streak, median gap, CI file parser, conventional-commit discipline scorer, phase-loop discipline (specs/plans/ADRs presence)

subsystems.name: Seed-driven generator pattern
subsystems.what: seed/repos.toml + seed/highlights.toml are the only operator-owned files; everything else is generated and overwritten. Clean separation: curated intent/why/domain framing drives generated prose without being touched by the generator

harvestable_assets.name: ETag-conditional GitHub REST client

harvestable_assets.why_reusable: Vendored from gridwork-core; needed in any Bun project making outbound HTTP. Low-cost insurance against hanging fetches.

harvestable_assets.name: Pure SVG chart library
harvestable_assets.what: 384-LOC library: stat cards, horizontal/vertical bar charts, heatmap matrix, Gantt timeline — all return standalone SVG strings, rasterizable via @resvg/resvg-js, zero runtime deps, deterministic output
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: Useful wherever server-side chart generation is needed without a headless browser (CI badges, reports, dashboards, email). The deterministic guarantee makes it testable.

harvestable_assets.name: Multi-language dependency + stack detector
harvestable_assets.what: 196-LOC module: parses package.json / pyproject.toml / requirements.txt into typed DepVersions; detects package manager, linter, formatter, bundler, monorepo tool, node/python version; infers monorepo architecture shape
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: Core of any repo-analytics, CI gating, or portfolio-indexing tool. Handles JS and Python in one pass with no external parser.

harvestable_assets.name: Commit cadence + CI + discipline analyzer
harvestable_assets.what: 117-LOC module: DOW/hour histograms, longest streak, median gap between commits, GitHub Actions workflow parser (triggers extraction), conventional-commit % scorer, presence check for specs/plans/ADRs
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: Surfaces developer workflow health signals without any external service. Useful for team dashboards, hiring analytics tools, or portfolio audits.

harvestable_assets.what: 93-LOC module: pairwise composite score = 0.5 * Jaccard(stack+deps) + 0.3 * Jaccard(domains) + 0.2 * cosine(workflow vector); union-find clustering at configurable threshold
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: Turns a flat list of repo profiles into a cluster map. Applicable to monorepo package grouping, template library organization, or code-reuse discovery.

harvestable_assets.name: Seed-driven generator pattern
harvestable_assets.what: TOML seed files hold operator-owned framing (domain, intent, why, source); the generator writes everything else and never touches seed. Supports local repos and https-only remote clone targets.

one_liner: A portfolio governor CLI for a solo founder: enforces four allocation laws (capacity, new-build gate, mode clarity, compounding protection) plus an operator-psychology signal layer over local repo telemetry, producing a single markdown screen refreshed via a weekly review ritual.

infra: local-only CLI (no server, no DB, no network except one loopback HTTP probe)

subsystems.name: Governor engine
subsystems.what: Pure-function governance: seed + telemetry + rules + operator signals → flags, capacity verdict, gate open/closed, operator weather panel. tools/lib/govern.ts (336 LOC).

subsystems.name: Zod schema layer
subsystems.what: All seed inputs (bets, rules, signals) validated at collect-time via strict Zod schemas; typed enums for modes, roles, revenue, bottleneck, load. tools/lib/schema.ts (258 LOC).

subsystems.name: Operator psychology signals
subsystems.what: TOML-driven failure-mode flags (exit_before_compounding, pre_revenue_desert, human_layer_rot, over_tooling, expression_gap) with per-signal antidotes surfaced on the screen. operator-profile/signals.toml + govern.ts.

subsystems.name: Snapshot / review-over-review diff
subsystems.what: Persists a slim projection per run to data/snapshots/<date>.json; diffs vs prior snapshot for 'Since last review' delta section. tools/lib/snapshot.ts (80 LOC).

subsystems.name: TOML-seed + generated-rollup pattern
subsystems.what: Operator owns seed/ (never overwritten); generator owns data/ and portfolio/ (always overwritten). Clean separation of subjective judgment from computed output. seed/bets.toml, tools/collect.ts, tools/render.ts.

subsystems.name: Sources adapters
subsystems.what: Read-only adapters for upstream sibling repos: dev-profile/data/profile.json (telemetry) and prospector/candidates/REGISTRY.md (inbound queue); plus one loopback HTTP probe for health-service freshness. tools/lib/sources.ts.

subsystems.name: Claude skills (review rituals)
subsystems.what: Three slash-command skills: /founder-review (weekly control loop), /founder-graduate (new-build gate ceremony), /operator-interview (one-question profile deepening). .claude/skills/.

harvestable_assets.name: Governor engine (govern.ts + schema.ts)
harvestable_assets.what: Pure-function governance core: takes typed seed + telemetry + rules + signals, returns flags, capacity, gate, weather. Zero external deps beyond Zod types.
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: The four-law pattern (capacity cap, new-build gate, mode-clarity staleness check, compounding-protection drift) is generic to any solo-founder or small-team portfolio governor. Drop in a new seed schema + rule dials and the logic adapts. 336 LOC, no side effects.

harvestable_assets.name: Zod seed + rules schema layer (schema.ts)
harvestable_assets.what: Strict Zod schemas for all hand-edited TOML inputs (BetSeedSchema, RulesSchema, SignalsSchema) plus all computed interface types (BetCard, Portfolio, Flag, Snapshot).
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: Self-contained type boundary with runtime validation — can be lifted directly into any template that follows the seed-as-config pattern. Enums (MODES, ROLES, REVENUE, BOTTLENECKS) are the vocabulary; rename slugs to adapt.

harvestable_assets.name: Operator psychology signal system
harvestable_assets.what: TOML-driven failure-mode → antidote map: named signals with enabled bool, severity, threshold dials, and declarative antidote prose surfaced on the rendered screen.
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: The signal.toml contract (enabled / severity / label / antidote) plus the govern.ts operatorSignalFlags() handler is a reusable pattern for any 'personalized AI assistant' that needs to fire psychology-aware flags. The schema is strict; adding a signal = one TOML stanza + one if-block in govern.ts.

harvestable_assets.name: Snapshot / delta diff module (snapshot.ts)
harvestable_assets.what: Persists a slim projection per run; diffs mode changes, flag raises/clears, momentum swings, gate flips, new inbound vs the prior snapshot.
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: The pattern — slim snapshot on every run, human-readable delta section — is applicable to any periodic report tool. Pure functions, ~80 LOC.

harvestable_assets.name: TOML-seed + generated-rollup CLI scaffold
harvestable_assets.what: bun run build pipeline: collect reads seed TOML + sibling-repo JSON → data/portfolio.json; render converts JSON → PORTFOLIO.md + per-bet cards. Generator owns generated files; operator owns seed.
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: The collect→render split with a JSON intermediate is a clean scaffold for any local-first report generator. The strict non-overwrite contract on seed/ is a design pattern worth extracting as a template convention.

harvestable_assets.name: Weekly review ritual skills (.claude/skills/)
harvestable_assets.what: Three Claude slash-command skills covering the full control loop: rebuild screen → walk five questions → re-steer seed → refresh operator profile → write dated review note.
harvestable_assets.why_reusable: The skill trio (review / graduate / interview) with the analyst-memo voice rule is a reusable pattern for any governance CLI that pairs a code layer with a weekly human-in-loop ritual. Low porting cost — mostly markdown.

Zod strict schema authorship at config/seed boundaries
TOML-driven operator-configurable rule dials (threshold changes in config, never hardcoded)

building_blocks.notes: The tiered pipeline design (tags → embeddings → captions → metadata) with an ANN index and provider-agnostic compute seam is a reusable architecture for any on-device AI media product. Not portable as code (Python pipeline is in tessera-public), but the ADRs + config pattern + compute seam design are strong architectural inspiration.

building_blocks.name: Biometric opt-in with erasure (BIPA/GDPR-aware)
building_blocks.notes: Off-by-default face recognition with explicit erasure satisfies the key BIPA/GDPR biometric data requirements. Pattern is portable as a checklist/scaffold for any consumer app adding face features. Moderate strength because the implementation is domain-specific (photo DAM) and the pattern is well-known — the value is in having it pre-implemented.

building_blocks.name: Hybrid SQLite vector + FTS search for local AI apps
building_blocks.notes: sqlite-vec + TurboVec ANN + FTS5 hybrid search over a local catalog is a reusable pattern for any local-first AI app needing semantic search without a hosted vector DB. Moderate because sqlite-vec + TurboVec are not yet battle-tested at very large scale and the integration is pipeline-specific.

building_blocks.name: Open-core pricing playbook for uncensored/adult-capable software
building_blocks.notes: LAUNCH.md documents a researched strategy for navigating adult-content payment processor and app-store restrictions while maintaining an open-core model. The AGPLv3 + CLA + offline-only Pro key framing avoids the platform ban triggers. Reusable as a strategy template for any 18+ capable tool.
